title: The night the Sun blacked out Quebec ⚡
subject: sun
description:
Would today's power grids survive a storm like this? 👇

On March 13, 1989, a geomagnetic storm caused by a solar eruption collapsed the Hydro-Québec grid, leaving 6 million people without power for about 9 hours. Auroras were seen as far south as Texas and Cuba.

Sources: NOAA NESDIS, "When Solar Storms Attack" (2015); Astronomy, "March 13, 1989: Quebec goes dark"; Space.com, "25 Years Ago: Amazing Auroras from 1989's Great Solar Storm" (2014); Wikipedia: March 1989 geomagnetic storm

scenes.text: The Sun blacked out 6 million people in 90 seconds.
At 2:45 a.m. on March 13, 1989, Quebec's power grid collapsed on a cold winter night.
Three days earlier, a huge flare had hurled charged gas straight at Earth.
It shook Earth's magnetic field and tripped breakers across Hydro-Québec's grid.
Auroras glowed as far south as Texas and Cuba. In the Cold War, some people feared a nuclear strike.
For 9 hours, 6 million people sat in the dark because of the Sun.
